scope acceptance requires existing oos-issue-cap fixtures to pass, but the plan tells the implementer to adapt expectations to current python behavior and explicitly preserve missing-input and same-input/output semantics that diverge from the bash harness. that drops fixture cases for missing-input failure, stale output cleanup on failure, in-place failure input preservation, and same input/output rejection. concretely, `issue_cap` treats a nonexistent `--input-file` as empty text and can return success (writing an empty `--output` or silently succeeding without output), contradicting the migrated missing-input fixture's fail-closed requirement once python becomes the only runtime.
